svg.title: A matrix is a picture of what it does
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing four unit squares transformed by a scale, a shear, a forty-five degree rotation and a rank-deficient squash that collapses the square onto a single red line, each with the image of the basis vectors drawn as a blue and a green arrow and the determinant written beneath; the determinant shown as the area of the transformed square going from one to four to zero; the three equivalent readings of a matrix product listed with numbered badges; a shape-check ladder where the inner dimensions of a batched matmul are ringed and joined; and a log-scaled bar chart of matmul throughput from 0.013 GFLOP per second for naive Python loops to 1550 for single-precision BLAS.
svg.text: A matrix is a picture of what it does
a LINE, not a square. det = 0
the COLUMNS are where the basis vectors land
det = the AREA of the transformed square
det = 0 -> flattened -> NO inverse. You cannot un-squash.
three ways to read A @ B - all the same numbers
row of A · column of B = one cell
each column of B, transformed by A
a sum of rank-1 outer products
reading 2 is the one that makes neural nets obvious
the shape check you do BEFORE you run it
these must MATCH, and then they VANISH
28,000x between your loop and BLAS. Do not write the loop.
Log scale - the real gap does not fit.
...and if the matrix squashes, what did it
